chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not eat while leaning since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him until He took his soul, and he used to eat the eating of a slave and sit the sitting of a slave. I said, 'And why was that?' He said, 'Out of humility for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.إِكْلَةَ الْعَبْدِ: The eating manner of a slave (sitting on the ground)
key_terms.جِلْسَةَ الْعَبْدِ: The sitting posture of a slave
key_terms.مُتَّكِئاً: Reclining or leaning back while eating

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) eat while sitting on the ground instead of reclining?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the Prophet's consistent humility in dining, noting he never ate while reclining from the time of his prophethood until his death. This practice of sitting in the manner of a servant (abd) serves as a profound model of tawaddu' (humility) for the Shia community, illustrating that spiritual status is maintained through modesty in mundane acts. It reinforces the concept that true nobility lies in servitude to God, a key theme in Twelver Shi'ite ethics.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zayd Al Shahaam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not eat whilst leaning since Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent him until he<sup>saww</sup> passed away, and he<sup>saww</sup> used to eat the eating of the slave, and he<sup>saww</sup> would sit the seating of a slave’. I said, ‘And why was that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In reverence to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Zayd al- Shahham who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, never ate while leaning against something from the day Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent him as the Messenger of Allah to the day he passed away. He (the Messenger of Allah) ate like a servant and sat like a servant.’ I then asked, ‘Why did he do so?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He did so to show humbleness before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.”’
